source.lapis_dirty_scope: Documentation and this sanitized evidence receipt only; runtime and verification source are committed.

scope: R1 first slice: an opt-in one-session headless birth broker behind LAPIS_BUILD_SUPERVISOR_RUNTIME. It adds no GUI, launchd, package, reboot, upgrade or multi-session behavior.

implementation.daemon: lapis_supervisor_daemon takes explicit absolute state-directory and control-endpoint paths, acquires the one-session registry, refuses persisted-session reconstruction and admits one first birth while its slot is empty.
implementation.request_contract: Strict version-1 JSON carries endpoint, fingerprint, agent mode, literal executable/arguments/cwd, geometry and an empty service environment. There is no caller service-program field.
implementation.reply_contract: A successful birth returns only supervisor-selected session ID and epoch. The spawn token is never returned.
implementation.service_selection: CMake supplies the pinned lapis_session_service executable; SessionServiceLauncher canonicalizes and fingerprint-checks the child before launch.
implementation.explicit_stop: SIGTERM performs the existing authenticated internal stop, terminates service and terminal ownership, removes endpoint/control sockets and leaves private stopped desired state.

observed: The daemon, real session service and /bin/cat terminal child ran as three distinct PIDs.
Hello preserved the terminal child PID while authoritative reconnect and a joined second client retained session identity.
Input echoed through both authoritative and joined v6 clients.
Malformed and oversized frames, nonempty environment, caller service-program shape, fingerprint mismatch and second active birth were refused.
Explicit stop removed the service ownership record and control endpoint and left a private stopped state record.

validation.name: focused-supervisor-daemon
validation.command: LAPIS_GHOSTTY_PREFIX=<validated pinned prefix> python3 -u scripts/check_supervisor_runtime.py --jobs 6 --output build/reports/r1-supervisor/receipt.json
validation.result: Configure, targeted build and state/runtime/real-service/daemon CTest passed. Both real-service and daemon integration markers were observed; neither was a bind skip.

validation.name: repository-quality
validation.result: Repository contracts, source/dirty receipts, diff hygiene, Ruff format/lint and Python unit tests passed.

validation.name: shared-cpp-gate
validation.command: LAPIS_GHOSTTY_PREFIX=<validated pinned prefix> python3 scripts/lapis.py check --jobs 6
validation.result: Dev configure/build/CTest, clang-format, Cppcheck and all clang-tidy shards passed.

validation.name: verification-runner-tools
validation.command: LAPIS_GHOSTTY_PREFIX=<validated pinned prefix> python3 scripts/lapis.py verify-tools
validation.result: All compiler, formatter, Cppcheck, clang-tidy, sanitizer and expected-failure tool fixtures passed.

repairs: Cppcheck now loads the Qt library and Q_MOC_INCLUDE definition in every analyzed mode; the prior dev-only configuration produced a false Q_ENUM unknown-macro failure.
The focused receipt now requires a distinct supervisor-daemon integration marker instead of accepting only the older real-service marker.

failed_attempts.result: The fresh worktree had no LAPIS_GHOSTTY_PREFIX and CMake correctly refused to configure.
failed_attempts.repair: A validated pinned prefix from the synchronized clean main checkout was selected explicitly; no source behavior was relaxed.

failed_attempts.result: Cppcheck reported an unknown Q_ENUM macro in unchanged Codex importer headers.
failed_attempts.repair: Qt metadata configuration was enabled for all analysis modes and the gate then passed.

non_claims: No GUI or CLI production birth route is implemented.
No launchd registration, daemon-restart reconstruction after a persisted session, package inclusion or update transition is implemented.
No credential-environment admission, real Codex/Claude launch, reboot, load, memory, latency or sanitizer workload is claimed by the daemon test.
The shared dev C++ gate does not build the opt-in supervisor target; the focused r1-runtime gate provides its compilation and behavioral coverage.
The harmless terminal child proves process and v6 ownership only; it is not agent-adapter qualification.
